author: GamingBolt
description:
A video game that uses awesome music to punctuate the story it's trying to tell sounds like a unique feature, doesn’t it? But even the greatest music cannot save a title that’s just boring to engage with. We’re happy to tell you that Mixtape doesn’t fall into that trap, and might even be a game that you look back on with a fond smile once you’re done with it.

With a great coming-of-age settibg that’s well-paced, a soundtrack that absolutely slaps, and a simple approach to its gameplay, Mixtape doesn’t push the boundaries of graphical fidelity or technical mastery. But what it does do is take you back to a bygone era in a way that’s quite hard to find in other titles. This is one tape you don’t want to miss, and might even find it hard to hit pause on. Join us as we tell you why that’s the case.
title: Mixtape Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
PSSR 2.0 is emerging as one of the most significant graphical upgrades for the PlayStation 5 Pro, quietly transforming how games look and perform. 

Instead of merely increasing resolution like traditional upscaling, 
PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution focuses on stabilizing image quality, reducing noise, and preserving fine detail all while maintaining strong frame-rate targets. 

This balance is increasingly important in modern titles, where players often must choose between graphical modes that prioritize visual fidelity or smooth performance. 

Although still relatively new, we are seeing many developers embrace the technology across a wide range of genres, from atmospheric horror to expansive open-world adventures. With this feature, we are putting the spotlight on 15 games that showcase great usage of PSSR 2.0  to enhance the overall gameplay experience.
title: Here’s How These 18 Games Used PSSR 2.0 To Max Out The PS5 Pro's Capabilities

author: GamingBolt
description:
Imagine that you work at a game studio. Aside from the layoffs, the boiler room exploding, and the long development cycles, it's not all that bad. Now imagine you're working at Rockstar North, which is leading development on Grand Theft Auto 6. “Long development cycles” is an understatement – this thing has been in the works since 2020 (along with an alleged reboot the same year, but we don't talk about that).

If those public records in the UK prove accurate, then salaries alone have already skyrocketed past $2.11 billion. “Triple-A”? The industry failed to make “Quadruple-A” a thing, but it's perhaps the most apt descriptor for your project.
title: GTA 6 Is So BIG That Even Rockstar Seems Nervous
